title: More Agents, More Reliable? System-Level Reliability of Multi-Agent LLMs under Operational-Profile Uncertainty
abstract: arXiv:2611.07140v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Teams increasingly build software from cooperating large language model (LLM) agents, often assuming more agents mean more reliability. Yet the usual evidence, average benchmark accuracy, ignores the input mix a deployed system meets and the rule merging the agents' answers. Building on HIP-LLM, a hierarchical imprecise-probability assessment of single LLMs, we propose a framework combining it with a Bayesian network of the system's failure logic for multi-agent systems. Agent failure-probability intervals propagate through this network, where the combining rule can itself fail, into a reliability envelope showing which evidence limits it. In a pipeline extracting regulated chemical-hazard statements, majority voting over three models protected against the weakest but did not clearly exceed the best, and a voter failing on 5\% of demands would largely erase its advantage over the middle model. translated_title: 更多智能体，更可靠吗？运行剖面不确定性下多智能体大语言模型系统的系统级可靠性
translated_abstract: 摘要：团队越来越多地基于协作的大语言模型（LLM）智能体来构建软件，并常常假设智能体越多意味着可靠性越高。然而，通常所依赖的证据——平均基准准确率——忽略了部署系统实际面对的输入分布（运行剖面）以及合并各智能体答案的规则。本文在HIP-LLM（一种针对单个LLM的分层不精确概率评估方法）的基础上，提出了一个将其与多智能体系统故障逻辑贝叶斯网络相结合的框架。各智能体的失效概率区间在该网络中传播——其中合并规则本身也可能失效——最终形成一个可靠性包络，用以显示是哪些证据限制了系统的可靠性。在一个提取受管制的化学品危害声明的流水线案例中，对三个模型进行多数投票可以防范最弱的模型，但并未明显超越最佳的单个模型；而如果一个投票者在5%的请求上失效，将基本抹去其相对中间水平模型的优势。更多的智能体能带来更可辩护的可靠性论证……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了将HIP-LLM单模型不精确概率评估与系统故障逻辑贝叶斯网络相结合的框架，用以在运行剖面不确定性下评估多智能体LLM系统的系统级可靠性，并揭示“更多智能体”并不必然更可靠——多数投票只能防范最弱模型，且投票者自身约5%的失效即可基本抵消其优势。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes a framework combining HIP-LLM's hierarchical imprecise-probability assessment of single LLMs with a Bayesian network of system failure logic to assess the system-level reliability of multi-agent LLM systems under operational-profile uncertainty, showing that more agents are not necessarily more reliable—majority voting only guards against the weakest model, and a voter failing on 5% of demands largely erases its advantage.
